findings.highlight: the tour documents
findings.evidenceJa: ツール関係はこのフォルダに入ってますから
findings.explanation: Haruki says the work-related tools or utilities are in the folder and their use is covered by the procedure manual. The English turns ツール into tour documents, inventing travel material.
findings.japanese:
「それで、ツール関係はこのフォルダに入ってますから。
使い方は手順書を見ればわかるようになってます」
findings.todokanai: "…And the tour documents are in this folder. I've set it up so you can find the instructions in these documents."

findings.highlight: thinking that no one else would accept such an assignment
findings.evidenceJa: 誰もが激しく拒否すると思ってた当の本人は、少し考え込む仕草を見せると、あっさり首を縦に振った
findings.explanation: Matsuoka is the very person everyone expected to reject the assignment fiercely; after a moment's thought, he simply nods. The English instead makes him think no one else would accept and then volunteer, inventing his motive.
findings.japanese:
その措置が決まった瞬間、
誰もが激しく拒否すると思ってた当の本人は、
少し考え込む仕草を見せると、あっさり首を縦に振った。
findings.todokanai: Once this measure was decided on, thinking that no one else would accept such an assignment, Matsuoka-san looked a bit deep in thought and eventually stepped forward.

findings.highlight: increasing the workload
findings.evidenceJa: しばらくはバイト増やして乗り切るしかない
findings.explanation: Hamada's temporary plan is to increase the number of part-time workers. The English says the department will increase the workload, the opposite of the proposed staffing relief.
findings.japanese:
「今、浜田さんが一生懸命人事と交渉してるけど、
しばらくはバイト増やして乗り切るしかないだろうって」
findings.todokanai: "Hamada-san is doing his best to come to a solution with HR, but for now, we'll have to live with increasing the workload."

findings.highlight: exclusively focused on work
findings.evidenceJa: 木崎さんはますます出先ばかり
findings.explanation: Kizaki is spending more and more of his time out of the office on assignments. The English turns his physical absence into the generic virtue of focusing exclusively on work.
findings.japanese:
浜田さんは部下に当たり散らすことが多くなり、
鈴木さんの雑談は消え、木崎さんはますます出先ばかり。
findings.todokanai: Hamada-san has become more irritable with his subordinates. Suzuki-san has stopped chatting, and Kizaki-san has been exclusively focused on work.

findings.highlight: the deadline for the Air Pocket
findings.evidenceJa: 締め切り後のエアポケットと相まって
findings.explanation: エアポケット is the lull or vacuum after a deadline, combining with the disappearance of conversation to make the office unnaturally quiet. The English parses Air Pocket as a publication whose deadline has passed.
findings.japanese:
そうやって編集部からどんどん会話が消えていき、
締め切り後のエアポケットと相まって、
ここが出版社とは思えない静けさに包まれている。
findings.todokanai: Couple the disappearance of chatter from the editing department with the passing of the deadline for the Air Pocket, and you would find the office so quiet that you could wonder whether this is a publishing office at all.

findings.highlight: I am the guest of honor at your farewell party
findings.evidenceJa: 一応、送別会の主賓だし
findings.explanation: Matsuoka says he will pay for Haruki's share because Haruki is the guest of honor. The English makes Matsuoka call himself the guest of honor at Haruki's farewell party.
findings.japanese:
「その代わり、お前の分は俺が出すから。
…一応、送別会の主賓だし」
findings.todokanai: "In exchange, I'll pay for your drink. I am the guest of honor at your farewell party, after all."

findings.highlight: when can I enter the venue tomorrow?
findings.evidenceJa: 明日、何時に会場入りだっけ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks what time Kazusa is due to enter the venue. The English has him ask when he is allowed to enter it.
findings.japanese:
「あ、それでさ…
明日、何時に会場入りだっけ？」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, by the way… when can I enter the venue tomorrow?"

findings.highlight: I'll begin by afternoon.
findings.evidenceJa: 昼過ぎには出るよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will leave after noon, which may cause her and Haruki to miss each other. 'I'll begin' does not state the departure that creates that possibility.
findings.japanese:
「昼過ぎには出るよ。
もしかしたら、すれ違いになるかもな」
findings.todokanai: "I'll begin by afternoon. We may end up passing each other."

findings.highlight: He's accepting my selfishness
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の身勝手のとばっちりを受けて、ずっと俺に厳しく当たっていた先輩とともに
findings.explanation: The sentence identifies Matsuoka as the senior who bore collateral damage from Haruki's selfishness and therefore treated him harshly. The English invents someone accepting Haruki's selfishness and leaves the relation to the senior incoherent.
findings.japanese:
俺の身勝手のとばっちりを受けて、
ずっと俺に厳しく当たっていた先輩とともに。
findings.todokanai: He's accepting my selfishness, along with the senior who was always so strict with me.

findings.highlight: It's my jealousy that ruined everything
findings.evidenceJa: 全部、あたしの独占欲がいけないんだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa first identifies her possessiveness—her need to have Haruki exclusively—as the cause, then names jealousy of Setsuna in the following line. The English collapses the first cause into jealousy and erases the deliberate progression.
findings.japanese: 「全部、あたしの独占欲がいけないんだ…」
findings.todokanai: "It's my jealousy that ruined everything…"

findings.highlight: he has been focused on nothing but his work
findings.evidenceJa: たまに顔を合わせても一言も会話がなくて、あからさまに避けられてたはずの先輩
findings.explanation: Haruki believed Kizaki had been openly avoiding him, saying nothing even when they happened to meet. The English reframes that social rejection as dedication to work and omits the explicit avoidance that makes Kizaki's arrival moving.
findings.japanese:
最近、ずっと出先ばかりで、
たまに顔を合わせても一言も会話がなくて、
あからさまに避けられてたはずの先輩が…
findings.todokanai: Recently, he has been focused on nothing but his work, and even when we passed each other by, he never said a word.

findings.highlight: the perfect person
findings.evidenceJa: 初めて会ったときから正しい人間だった
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Setsuna a righteous or morally correct person from the moment they met. 'Perfect person' changes the specific moral quality that frightened and dazzled Kazusa into general flawlessness.
findings.japanese:
「お前は、初めて会ったときから正しい人間だった。
春希と同じ…ううん、
あいつ以上にまっすぐで、強かった」
findings.todokanai: "You were the perfect person from the moment we met. You were strong and straightforward, just like… no, even more than Haruki."

findings.highlight: "I know it's not the right thing to do. I know no one will accept it. But I can't help myself from betraying you."
findings.evidenceJa:
「悪いことだってわかってる。
許されないって知ってる。
けど、裏切らずにはいられないんだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she knows the betrayal cannot be forgiven; 'no one will accept it' changes forgiveness into social acceptance — Her moral recognition that the act is wrong and her inability to stop are explicit.
findings.japanese:
「悪いことだってわかってる。
許されないって知ってる。
けど、裏切らずにはいられないんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I know it's not the right thing to do. I know no one will accept it. But I can't help myself from betraying you."

findings.highlight: I think.
findings.evidenceJa: 持ってる。どっちの部屋のも
findings.explanation: Kazusa states that she has the keys to both apartments. The English adds uncertainty, misleadingly suggesting she may be unsure whether she has them when the scene's question is why she chose to wait outside despite certainly having access.
findings.japanese:
「あ、ええと…持ってる。
どっちの部屋のも」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, I have the keys for both apartments… I think."

findings.highlight: I grab onto her hands and let out an anguished expression
findings.evidenceJa: とうとう俺に、手のひらを掴まれ、苦悶の表情を浮かべ
findings.explanation: Kazusa has her palms seized by Haruki and shows an anguished expression. The English assigns that expression to Haruki.
findings.japanese:
とうとう俺に、手のひらを掴まれ、
苦悶の表情を浮かべ…
findings.todokanai: Eventually, I grab onto her hands and let out an anguished expression…

findings.highlight: I was holding on to your hand before I even realized it.
findings.evidenceJa: 気がついたら振り払ってた。あなたの愚かな真似を、必死で止めてた
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that before she knew it she had knocked or swept away Kazusa's attempted act and was desperately stopping the foolish self-injury. The English invents her holding Kazusa's hand, obscuring the physical interruption that caused the glass to fall.
findings.japanese:
「だからわからないんだよ！
気がついたら振り払ってた。
あなたの愚かな真似を、必死で止めてた」
findings.todokanai: "I just said I don't know! I was holding on to your hand before I even realized it. I was desperately trying to stop your idiotic act."

findings.highlight: including the smell of alcohol
findings.evidenceJa: むせ返るようなアルコール臭の中、ほんのわずかな俺の匂いを逃すまいとするように
findings.explanation: Amid Haruki's overpowering reek of alcohol, Kazusa presses close as if determined not to miss the faint trace of his own scent. The English says the alcohol smell is included among the scents she is trying to preserve, reversing the contrast.
findings.japanese:
むせ返るようなアルコール臭の中、
ほんのわずかな俺の匂いを逃すまいとするように。
findings.todokanai: Almost as if trying to keep the smell of me from escaping, including the smell of alcohol.

findings.highlight: Setsuna would completely break down
findings.evidenceJa: それがますます雪菜を追い込み、どうしようもなく決裂してしまう
findings.explanation: Kazusa's intervention would drive Setsuna further into a corner and make an irreparable rupture between the two women inevitable. The English replaces the rupture of their relationship with Setsuna personally breaking down.
findings.japanese:
それがますます雪菜を追い込み、
どうしようもなく決裂してしまうなんて、
火を見るより明らかだったのに。
findings.todokanai: In the end, she only made things worse for Setsuna. It was plain as day from the start that Setsuna would completely break down.

findings.highlight: her overestimating herself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に対しての過大評価…というか、あまりの想いの深さ
findings.explanation: The narrator Haruki leaves unmentioned Kazusa's excessive valuation of him—or rather, the overwhelming depth of her feelings for him. The English instead says Kazusa overestimates herself, reversing the object of valuation.
findings.japanese:
この際、自分に対しての過大評価…というか、
あまりの想いの深さには触れないままにしておく。
findings.todokanai: I have some words about her overestimating herself… but right now, I won't touch on any subject heavy in emotion.

findings.highlight: allow myself to be restrained
findings.evidenceJa: 余計にかずさの温もりを感じてしまうという甘い制裁を俺に科す
findings.explanation: By loosening his grip and embracing Kazusa gently, Haruki imposes on himself the sweet punishment of feeling her warmth even more intensely. The English invents restraint and omits both punishment and heightened warmth.
findings.japanese:
余計にかずさの温もりを感じてしまうという
甘い制裁を俺に科す。
findings.todokanai: I feel her warmth. And allow myself to be restrained.

findings.highlight: She refused to admit I was wrong
findings.evidenceJa: 最後の最後でどうしようもなく優しくて、見誤って、手を離して、足を止めて
findings.explanation: Kazusa lists Setsuna's terminal kindness and the actions born of her misjudgment: letting go and stopping. The English invents Setsuna refusing to admit Kazusa was wrong, assigning an object and moral claim absent from 見誤って.
findings.japanese:
「でもあいつ、最後の最後でどうしようもなく優しくて、
見誤って、手を離して、足を止めて…」
findings.todokanai: "But she was hopelessly kind to me, even up until the very end. She refused to admit I was wrong, she let go of my hand, and she stopped me in my tracks…"

findings.highlight: quarrel, and get sick of each other
findings.evidenceJa: 傷ついて、傷つけられて、疲れてもまだ、息ができないほどの恋に、落ちていこう
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes that even after hurting and being hurt, even when exhausted, they keep falling into a love so intense they cannot breathe. The English changes reciprocal wounds into quarrelling and changes exhaustion into becoming sick of each other.
findings.japanese:
傷ついて、傷つけられて、疲れてもまだ、
息ができないほどの恋に、落ちていこう…
findings.todokanai: Let's overwhelm ourselves in a love so powerful that we can get hurt, quarrel, and get sick of each other, and still go on despite that.

findings.highlight: will it one day reflect back to me
findings.evidenceJa: 届かない恋をしていても
findings.explanation: The lyric asks whether, even while loving beyond reach, a day will come when that love can be shown or brought into view. 'Reflect back to me' invents a reflexive return and obscures the load-bearing song phrase 届かない恋.
findings.japanese:
「届かない恋をしていても…
映し出す日が来るかな…」
findings.todokanai: "Even if my love can't reach you… will it one day reflect back to me…?"
